title: Chumor 2.0: Towards Better Benchmarking Chinese Humor Understanding from (Ruo Zhi Ba)

model.params_source: assumed (paper silent); snapshot by the post-2024-07 alias rule (record)

items.source: MichiganNLP/Chumor (test.tsv; gated with automatic approval after login)

fields_paper.label: human label: fully explains vs partially/does not explain (column name unverified)

prompt.source_location: Appendix F 'Prompts for DP and CoT in Chumor', Direct Prompting (DP); also Sec. 4.1
prompt.verbatim: full (spurious intra-character spaces produced by justified typesetting in the extraction removed)

output.parse: label from set [完全解释, 部分/没有解释]
output.postprocess: strip; if both or neither label string occurs, count as incorrect
output.parse_paper: label from set [完全解释, 部分/没有解释] by substring match

metric.name: accuracy
metric.definition: share of instances whose predicted label equals the human label, in percent
metric.original_location: Table 4 (Appendix H), row GPT-4turbo, column DP ACC (MCC 0.20)

cost.prepare_note: not prepared (source gated / archive / unreachable / >100 MB)

open_points: gated dataset: the parquet URL and the datasets-server both return HTTP 401 without a logged-in token (gated 'auto'), so the column names (joke, explanation, label) and the label vocabulary are still unverified; the parquet listing itself is visible (default/test)
runner note: 'label from set' uses \w word boundaries, which fail when a Chinese label is embedded in running text (e.g. 该解释完全解释了笑话); the paper's substring match would be needed
notes: Jokes plus explanations make the input ~600 tokens (~$0.008 per call). The label 'fully explain' is the positive class for MCC/FPR/FNR in Table 4.
